releases.name: v0.9.0 — Gemini Web backend 4.27, AI Studio 0.2.19, image input on by default
releases.body:
## Backends

- **Gemini Web backend [4.27.0-magpie.1](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/releases/tag/backend-v4.27.0-magpie.1)**, based on upstream v4.27.0. Tool calls whose arguments contain ``` are no longer cut short, and network errors no longer count against a cookie. Accounts signed in alongside others in one browser can be given an account number (`authuser`). Chats keep the silence-based timing from 4.26.0-magpie.2: upstream's new `web_channel` transport is locked off until it supports that. The usage card reads accounts with an account number from that account's own Gemini page. (#42)
- **Managed AI Studio [0.2.19-magpie.1](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/releases/tag/studio-v0.2.19-magpie.1)**, based on upstream v0.2.19. It adds retries for broken function calls and dropped streams, schema fixes, SpiderMonkey heap shrinking and HTTP/2 connection reuse. Settings saved in the admin page survive the upgrade, account bindings and hedge model selections are kept, and hedge requests stay off by default. (#39)

## Changes

- **Image input is on by default for Gemini Web**, as it already was for AI Studio. Turn it off with `magpie plugin options magpie-gemini-web '{"allowImages":false}'`. (#41)
- **AI Studio service information shows as text.** The proxy and admin-page descriptions no longer appear as permanent "100% remaining" meters; real model cooldowns keep their percentages and reset times. (#38)

## Upgrade

Install the attached `magpie-gemini-web-0.9.0.tgz` or update the plugin through your usual workflow. Running backends are not interrupted. Stop the managed Gemini Web backend (its PID is in `backend.pid` in the data directory) and the AI Studio service, and the next managed start upgrades each one. Configuration, credentials and accounts are kept.

From AI Studio 0.2.18: if you had turned on `FIRST_EVENT_HEDGE=auto`, it now covers only the models in `FIRST_EVENT_HEDGE_MODELS` (`gemini-4-argon` unless you choose more in the admin page).

## Validation

- All 212 JavaScript tests passed on the release commit.
- All 52 files in the attached package were verified against commit `54a4c223c28d1a14849de492f364ab961824c28b`.
- Both backends were downloaded from their public release URLs and smoke-tested on darwin-arm64: checksum, install, startup and authentication. The Gemini Web backend also passed proxy binding and reuse. AI Studio also passed settings across a restart, managed update refusal and a clean stop. Build provenance and the per-platform verification runs are in the linked backend releases.
- Gemini Web 4.27.0-magpie.1 has not yet answered a live signed-in request.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/compare/v0.8.1...v0.9.0

releases.name: AI Studio 0.2.19-magpie.1
releases.body:
AI Studio backend based on upstream v0.2.19, managed exclusively by the Magpie plugin.

- **Upstream v0.2.19**: retries malformed function calls, dropped streams and trailing 5xx errors when no output has been sent yet. It also fixes complex schemas, shrinks the SpiderMonkey heap and reuses HTTP/2 connections. Camoufox, the SpiderMonkey static libraries and the pinned toolchains are unchanged from 0.2.18.
- **Saved settings are preserved** (`patches/studio-0.2.19-managed-config.patch`, SHA-256 `fa7be4b0d25d529849fe5ce2979e3b5db74487878a7f809db833b3d422349e98`). Upstream 0.2.19 migrates legacy settings and leaves values that equal the defaults out of `.env`. That would overwrite explicit hedge and timeout choices, and the plugin would reset its saved defaults on the next start. When built with `internal/config.managedBy=magpie-gemini-web`, the backend skips the legacy `.env` rewrite and saves every editable setting explicitly. Settings owned by the environment stay locked.
- **New settings**: `API_KEY_ACCOUNTS` (account bindings) and `FIRST_EVENT_HEDGE_MODELS` keep what the admin page saved and ignore same-named host variables. Upstream defaults `FIRST_EVENT_HEDGE` to `auto`. The plugin writes `off` when it isn't set, so hedge requests stay off by default and upgrading doesn't use more quota. Users who already had `FIRST_EVENT_HEDGE=auto` should check its model list: in 0.2.19 it covers only `FIRST_EVENT_HEDGE_MODELS`, which is `gemini-4-argon` unless more are chosen.
- Safe request-body migration (`patches/studio-0.2.17-preserve-request-bodies.patch`, SHA-256 `4cdafbe2c1fb9c2fa913c15845257e0a16bbfa406fb7dc11d0a5bf1eaaa996a0`) is unchanged.
- WAA still runs on SpiderMonkey (`WAA_BACKEND=spidermonkey`), so generation needs no browser; Camoufox is only for Google sign-in. Update checks return local managed status without contacting GitHub, and installing an update returns HTTP 409.

Source: upstream commit `0451f26248b7ce263a4fdbf92b280897cb79d74f` (v0.2.19) plus the two patches above. Go 1.27.1, Camoufox 152.0.4-beta.29, SpiderMonkey v152.0.4-aistudio2api.1, Zig 0.16.0 (Linux), llvm-mingw 20261020 (Windows), Xcode 26.3 (macOS). Build instructions: `docs/studio-release.md`.

Validation: all five native runners in [the verification workflow](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/41569441959) passed at the release commit `54a4c223c28d1a14849de492f364ab961824c28b`. Each one rebuilt the pinned source, passed upstream tests, matched the archive and executable SHA-256, installed the real archive with isolated data (admin settings saved across a restart, managed update status, HTTP 409 on update, stop), and passed the plugin tests with that archive. The archives were uploaded by [the upload workflow](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/41570898711), which checks every pin first. Live checks before merge ([#39](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/pull/39)), on the CI darwin-arm64 archive with a signed-in account, passed. Magpie refreshed its models, tested Argon, and kept six admin settings across a full restart. Nine gateway checks passed, among them tool calls, cancellation and resuming after a backend restart. `generate_image` returned a 1376×768 image. Google sign-in and re-login through Camoufox were not exercised.

These are backend assets consumed by the magpie-gemini-web plugin release, not the npm plugin package.

releases.name: Optimized backend 4.27.0-magpie.1
releases.body:
Ready-to-run optimized backend for **macOS, Linux and Windows, on x64 and arm64**, built from upstream v4.27.0 with `patches/argon.patch`. The next plugin release selects these assets by default during one-click setup.

New in this backend:

- **Upstream v4.27.0.** Accounts signed in to the same browser as other accounts can be given an account number (`authuser`, the `N` in `/u/N/`), so chats, uploads and downloads use that account rather than the default one. Tool calls whose arguments contain ``` are no longer cut short (upstream #65). A network error while fetching the sign-in token no longer counts against the cookie. When every proxy is circuit-broken the error is now `proxy_unavailable`. Generated images can be fetched at full size with `image_upscale` (off by default).
- Our patch carries `authuser` through the cancellable upload, the long-prompt context file and the XSRF cache, including its background refresh. A call whose arguments contain ``` still finishes early as soon as its outer fence closes.
- **Chats stay on StreamGenerate.** Upstream's new `web_channel` transport (processSession) is locked off in this build. It doesn't yet have silence timing ([#33](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/issues/33)), client-cancel propagation, the early tool-call finish or extended thinking. A config that turns it on is logged and ignored, and the panel switch is removed.
- Everything from 4.26.0-magpie.2 carries over: silence-based chat timing (180 s of silence by default), bounded connect and handshake waits, XSRF caching, cancellation propagation and Argon model verification.

## Build provenance

- Upstream: [zexadev/gemini-web2api-go@e97cfcc](https://github.com/zexadev/gemini-web2api-go/commit/e97cfccc7e68e356ac504ba220e0b004382029a8)
- Patch SHA-256: `865ae5390072cc003bfa28dc61e8a9136e5a30bc3b9b68b352f8a0d0e91fcc85`
- Go: `1.27.1`, `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `-trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags="-s -w"`
- Reported backend version: `4.27.0-magpie.1`
- Included: six executables, patched source archive, `build.json`, `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and the upstream MIT license.

The installer pins each executable's SHA-256 in `lib/backend-release.json`. Existing published assets must not be overwritten because installed plugin versions rely on those hashes.

## Validation

All seven jobs in [the release verification workflow](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/41569437441) passed at the release commit `54a4c223c28d1a14849de492f364ab961824c28b`. Each of the six native OS/architecture runners rebuilt the pinned sources, passed Go tests, matched the pinned SHA-256, and installed and started its real executable with isolated data, including the proxy-binding check. The plugin's 212 JavaScript tests passed. The executables were uploaded by [the upload workflow](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/41569973976), which checks every pin first, and every asset here matches `SHA256SUMS.txt`. These checks used no Google credentials.

Not yet checked against Google: this build has not answered a live signed-in request. The request path for default accounts is the one 4.26.0-magpie.2 used, but if something goes wrong, `npm run backend:install:upstream` or reinstalling plugin 0.8.1 goes back.

## Upgrade and rollback

A running backend is left alone. Stop it before upgrading (the managed process ID is in the data directory's `backend.pid`). The next automatic start upgrades a stopped official backend and keeps its configuration, credentials and account database.

From the plugin directory, with the backend stopped:

```bash
npm run backend:install           # select this optimized release
npm run backend:install:upstream  # select the pinned official v4.27.0
```

The selected channel persists across automatic starts. If a download or checksum check fails, the existing binary is kept.

releases.name: v0.8.1 — Gemini Web waits out Google's queue; usage refresh shows current figures
releases.body:
## Fixes

- **Gemini Web waits through Google's queue.** The bundled backend is now [4.26.0-magpie.2](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/releases/tag/backend-v4.26.0-magpie.2). Chat requests time out after 180 seconds of silence by default, rather than 180 seconds of total elapsed time. Google's queue heartbeats keep the request alive, and replies that keep streaming are no longer cut off. The plugin's default Gemini Web backend wait increases to 570 seconds; explicit timeout settings still take precedence. Direct and proxied connections also have bounded connection/handshake waits. (#33, #36)
- **Usage refresh shows current figures.** When Magpie requests usage, account readings at least 30 seconds old are fetched from Google again, including usage from the Gemini app, website, and other devices. Concurrent reads are shared. Failed reads normally back off for 10 minutes, with an early retry when Magpie asks again within a minute. (#34, #35)

## Documentation

- Explain how agents can use AI Studio image models for image generation and reference images. (#32)
- Clarify the default concurrency: Gemini Web allows two requests per sign-in, AI Studio one.

## Upgrade

Install the attached `magpie-gemini-web-0.8.1.tgz` or update the plugin through your usual workflow. A running Gemini Web backend is not interrupted automatically: stop the existing managed backend (its PID is in `backend.pid` in the data directory), then the next managed startup upgrades it while preserving configuration and credentials.

## Validation

- All 212 JavaScript tests passed on the release commit.
- All 51 files in the attached package were verified against commit `b6f3cfb40a560dac5a64b422b72e7237dfb3c407`.
- Backend build provenance and platform verification are documented in the linked backend release.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/compare/v0.8.0...v0.8.1

releases.name: Optimized backend 4.26.0-magpie.2
releases.body:
Ready-to-run optimized backend for **macOS, Linux and Windows, on x64 and arm64**, built from upstream v4.26.0 with `patches/argon.patch`. The next plugin release selects these assets by default during one-click setup.

New in this backend:

- Chat requests are timed by silence, not by their whole length. Gemini Web queues a request for minutes before its first words (3.6 Flash took 48 to 393 s in our runs) and sends a 38-byte heartbeat every 60 s while it waits. The old 180 s whole-request limit cut off every request queued longer than that and retried it from the back of the queue, and the third try failed at 544 s ([#33](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/issues/33)); it also cut off replies still coming at 180 s. A try is now given up, and retried, only after Google has sent nothing for `request_timeout_sec` (180 s by default: three missed heartbeats). Page loads, uploads and other requests keep their whole-request limit.
- Direct connections to Google have their own limits: 30 s to connect, and the connection is dropped if Google sends nothing within 10 s of it opening. tls-client redials a dropped HTTP/2 connection without the request's context, so a server that accepted the connection and never answered could stall requests until the backend restarted. Proxied connections get a 10 s TLS handshake limit.

## Build provenance

- Upstream: [zexadev/gemini-web2api-go@7ce02d8](https://github.com/zexadev/gemini-web2api-go/commit/7ce02d89512058b2bd147fb2dc4e40187f5135ad)
- Patch SHA-256: `c0697c8382db912b545ed11394e67a998a55393bb1f81e86f6fb2400c150dccb`
- Go: `1.27.1`, `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `-trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags="-s -w"`
- Reported backend version: `4.26.0-magpie.2`
- Included: six executables, patched source archive, `build.json`, `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and the upstream MIT license.

The installer pins each executable's SHA-256 in `lib/backend-release.json`. Existing published assets must not be overwritten because installed plugin versions rely on those hashes.

## Validation

All seven jobs in [the release verification workflow](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/41279136190) passed. Each of the six native OS/architecture runners rebuilt the pinned sources, passed Go tests, matched the published SHA-256, and installed and started its real executable with isolated data, including the proxy-binding check. The plugin's 211 JavaScript tests passed. These checks used no Google credentials.

Live checks on one account: with silence timing, requests queued for 393 s and 188 s were answered (the longest silence while queued was about 60 s). An anonymous page load from gemini.google.com through the new dialer worked over HTTP/2, including after a forced redial.

## Upgrade and rollback

A running backend is left alone. Stop it before upgrading (the managed process ID is in the data directory's `backend.pid`); the next automatic start upgrades a stopped official backend and keeps configuration, credentials and the account database.

From the plugin directory, with the backend stopped:

```bash
npm run backend:install           # select this optimized release
npm run backend:install:upstream  # select the pinned official v4.26.0
```

The selected channel persists across automatic starts. Failed downloads or checksum verification preserve the existing binary.
